title: Senior Full-Stack Engineer (Go + TypeScript)
description: Company Overview hermeneutic research is a best-in-class proprietary trading firm and hedge fund. It deploys research-driven discretionary and systematic strategies as well as makes strategic long-term investments. The partners' decade-long history of success in trading and business building and a firm-wide cultural emphasis on alpha generation, open debate, relentless iteration, and teamwork are key to the firm's continued expansion in a challenging market environment that has hamstrung competitors. A hard-wired emphasis on risk management and opportunistic market participation ensure that hermeneutic research will continue its growth trajectory in the coming decades. Job Overview We are seeking experienced full-stack engineers to build the user interfaces and services for mission-critical financial applications: visual analytics platforms and data-driven tools used by traders, researchers, and analysts. You will work on the TypeScript front-ends and the Go services that serve them. We are evolving our front-end applications into a modular, plugin-based platform that other engineers and teams build on—so you will build reusable UI modules, component libraries, and SDKs as much as end-user features, and also the Go services that ingest, process, and serve market and on-chain data to these applications. You will own your work from structured product requirements through to production. This is a highly collaborative role in a fast-paced environment where clean design, high performance, and responsive UIs are critical to the business. You don't need a background in trading or finance. We care most about engineering craft and will teach you the domain. Responsibilities Collaborate with traders, researchers, and product managers to translate complex workflows into elegant UI solutions. Design and implement high-performance, responsive front-end applications using a current-generation TypeScript framework (Svelte, React, or Vue). Design, build and operate Go back-end services with security and performance considerations baked into their design. Own service boundaries and data contracts end-to-end, from Go services to typed front-end SDKs. Build reusable UI modules, component libraries, and SDKs for a modular, plugin-based UI platform. Build real-time UIs that ingest and render high-frequency market and on-chain data from multiple streaming sources. Develop high-performance data visualizations for large, fast-updating datasets, using canvas-based charting (e.g. uPlot, TradingView Lightweight Charts) and D3.js for bespoke views. Integrate the front-end with back-end services through typed SDKs and MCP-based interfaces, including real-time market and on-chain data. Drive architecture and performance decisions for modular, extensible systems, with scalability and maintainability in mind. Deploy and maintain applications, keeping them reliable and performant under heavy load. Write and maintain automated tests and take part in code review to keep the codebase reliable and maintainable. Support system maintenance and feature evolution with a high delivery cadence and short iteration cycles. Mentor other engineers and promote engineering best practices across the team. Requirements Must Have 7+ years of hands-on full-stack development, with production ownership on both back-end and front-end. Strong, current TypeScript, HTML, CSS, and one or more modern front-end frameworks (Svelte, React, or Vue), with the adaptability to work primarily in the framework a team has chosen rather than staying tied to one. Strong, current Go experience, able to design, build and operate production Go services independently. Experience building reusable, well-structured UI components and shared abstractions. Proven experience handling large datasets and real-time updates from back-end sources (WebSockets, Server-Sent Events). Strong understanding of performance optimization and rendering strategies in data-heavy applications, including a solid grasp of the JavaScript runtime. Solid testing discipline, with unit and integration tests as a normal part of delivery. Genuine UI/UX sensibility—you can tell a polished interface from a rough one, and care about the difference. Familiarity with cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, or Azure) and version control. Excellent communication and collaboration in a cross-functional team. Nice to Have Background or strong interest in trading systems or financial platforms. Exceptional design taste / portfolio-grade UI work. Experience with relational databases, data warehouses, and caching strategies. Experience with real-time or on-chain / crypto market data. Experience with MCP (Model Context Protocol) or other AI-native / agent integration. Experience building developer platforms, SDKs, or shared component libraries used by other engineers. Understanding of microservice architectures, continuous delivery, and zero-downtime deployment. Experience with CI/CD pipelines, Docker, and observability tools such as Datadog, Grafana, or ELK. Prior work in hedge funds, proprietary trading, or similar finance environments. Interview Process CV Screening – We will review your application based on the qualifications and experience outlined above. Phone Screening – A screening session with a few on-the-spot technical questions to assess your fundamental knowledge and problem-solving approach. Assignment – A take-home assignment to demonstrate your approach, critical thinking, and relevant skills. Assignment Review – A discussion of your assignment, focusing on your approach, reasoning, and solutions. CTO Interview – Interview with the CTO to discuss your experience, technical expertise, problem-solving approach, and overall fit for the role. Co-Founder Interview – A concluding discussion to evaluate cultural fit, strategic alignment, and how you resonate with the firm’s values. Company Values Throughout the process, you'll be assessed for cultural fit through our company values: Drive – We believe the best team members are deeply passionate about what they do. That passion fuels their growth, drives them to seek out the best teams, and leads them to hold high expectations of themselves in pursuit of excellence. Ownership – We aim to extend ownership as broadly as possible across the firm. In return, we value people who take initiative, step up when needed, and treat the company’s goals as their own. Judgment – We value those who see the big picture and focus on what truly drives impact and results. They use time wisely, adapt across domains, and always prioritize outcomes over comfort zones. Openness – We foster a culture of open communication, mutual challenge, and shared growth. We believe constructive debate and proactive knowledge sharing lead us closer to the truth—and better decisions. Competence – We work with people who bring exceptional intellectual strength. What sets them apart isn’t just what they know—it’s how they use what they know to navigate change, adapt quickly, and contribute meaningfully in fast-changing environments. Resilience – We perform under pressure. Markets move fast, and so do we—but we stay grounded, focused, and calm. We embrace uncertainty, learn from setbacks, and adapt quickly without losing sight of long-term goals. Originally posted on Himalayas

Review payroll inputs and outputs for accuracy and completeness. Support new hires, terminations, compensation changes, deductions, taxes, and one-time payments. Help standardize payroll practices while accounting for local requirements. Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Business Administration, Finance, or a related field Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills. Experience supporting acquisitions, payroll conversions, or a global workforce. Excellent organization, analytical ability, and attention to detail. Ability to investigate discrepancies and clearly communicate findings. Comfort working across multiple companies, countries, currencies, and time zones. Openly Self-Critical: Leaders go first: they surface their misses early, ask for direct feedback, and turn “game film” into better decisions and better systems. Mutual Elevation: Committed to growth, elevating teams, developing future leaders, and removing barriers to mastery and joy. Learn-it-alls: Learn-it-alls, not know-it-alls, embracing failure as part of growth and progress. Pioneering: Pioneering driven by opportunity, using first principles thinking and unbound by tradition or rules. Will to Win: Leaders relentlessly pursue potential, reject mediocrity, and get what they tolerate. Dialectical: We learn through conversation. We ask, listen, question, and evolve — valuing disagreement as a tool for alignment and deeper understanding. Frugality: Achieving more with less, focusing on quality, long-term value, and company-wide responsibility. Candor: We communicate with integrity, transparency, and respect in all conversations. Kaizen: Kaizen is continuous improvement as a way of life. Leaders make hundreds of small upgrades that compound, turning lessons into standards and standards into durable systems. title: AI Product Engineer
description: Working Schedule: Monday – Friday, 8am – 5pm Mountain Standard Time Work Arrangement: Fully Remote Salary: 2,000 - 2,500 USD Employer: AI company located in Phoenix, Arizona The Role This is a new kind of engineering role. You won't be a code monkey wired into a backlog. You'll own features end-to-end using Claude Code and other coding agents: design, implementation, testing, shipping. You direct the AI, you read every line it produces, and you ship the finished thing. You'll work across the platform: Threo (the client workspace), Wingtip (agentic execution from plain English requests), Pylon (agent creation and runtime), and Canopy (the control plane for every client tenant). Our stack spans .NET/C# and FastAPI (Python) on the backend, React on the frontend, and PostgreSQL for data. You don't need to know it all on day one — you need to ramp fast with coding agents and ship in stacks you haven't touched before. We hire for taste and velocity. What You'll Do Take a problem from rough idea to shipped feature: design, build, test, deploy, working from specs and repo-level agent instructions you and your agents both use. No handoffs for "the real implementation." Read every line the AI produces. You're accountable for what ships, not the model. Operate two, three, or more AI agents at once across separate work streams (new features, bug fixes, refactors), keeping each in its own sandbox or work tree and shipping from all of them the same day without losing state or scope. Ship services in .NET 10 LTS / C# (ASP.NET Core, Minimal APIs, background workers). Build and extend Python services using FastAPI for our agent execution engine and adjacent tooling. Design and evolve data models in PostgreSQL: schema, migrations, indexes, query performance. Build React 19 interfaces with the stable React Compiler — admin consoles, data grids, forms, and chat UIs. Implement streaming chat and live updates, and integrate with LLM providers via tool calling and MCP servers, structured outputs, retries, and fallbacks. Write tests, write docs, close the loop, and debug across services and stacks — the AI helps, but it doesn't excuse you from understanding the system. The bar is "that's done," not "the happy path works." Ship via Docker and GitHub Actions to our cloud infrastructure. What We're Looking For We hire on AI fluency, judgment, and velocity, not years of experience. If you live in Claude Code (or Cursor, or Codex) and ship real software with it, we want to talk. Must Have Daily, fluent use of agentic coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or similar). We care that you can direct an agent through a non-trivial feature without losing the plot — not which tool you use — and that your first instinct is to design with AI in the loop. Parallel agent management. You can run multiple agents at once across separate work streams (features, bug fixes, refactors) and deliver shipped work from each. Solid programming fundamentals. title: Principal Backend Architect
description: Principal Backend Architect (C#/.NET, Azure) Location: Remote from Latin America Compensation: $45–$52 USD per hour Engagement: Full-time international independent contractor About Latino Legends Latino Legends connects exceptional Latin American talent with international companies building and scaling high-performing remote teams. We partner with companies across the US, Canada, the UK, and Australia to match skilled professionals with opportunities where they can make a meaningful impact. About the Role Our client is a US-based software company with an engineering team of approximately 30 people, supporting a large monolithic platform alongside a growing ecosystem of microservices. With dedicated architects for frontend and data, they are looking for a Principal Backend Architect / Engineer to take ownership of the backend architecture, the most extensive and business-critical part of their platform. In this role, you'll shape the architecture of the backend ecosystem, including the monolith, microservices, APIs, messaging infrastructure, and integrations. You'll establish engineering standards, guide the platform's evolution toward well-defined services, and remain hands-on with implementation to ensure architectural decisions translate into reliable, scalable production systems. You'll work closely with the Lead/Principal Architect, Principal UI Architect, and Data Architect to drive technical direction across the platform. This is a principal-level individual contributor role , ideal for an experienced engineer who combines architectural ownership with strong technical execution. There are no direct reports, and hands-on development remains a core part of the position. Key Responsibilities Own backend architecture across the platform and lead the incremental decomposition of a large monolith into well-defined, maintainable services. Establish backend engineering standards, best practices, and tooling, including shared libraries, service templates, and cross-cutting platform capabilities. Lead API and contract design, ensuring effective versioning, backward compatibility, and reliable communication between internal services, frontend applications, and external integrations. Own event-driven architecture using Azure Service Bus, including message delivery guarantees, retries, idempotency, and failure recovery. Define scalable patterns for customer and partner integrations, ensuring failures are observable, traceable, and recoverable. Collaborate with the Data Architect on data ownership, transactional boundaries, access patterns, and query performance. Improve platform reliability, security, observability, and cloud cost efficiency. Champion AI-assisted engineering practices and help expand the team's capabilities through practical adoption of AI tools and workflows. Mentor engineers, review critical pull requests, facilitate technical office hours, and document architectural decisions through Architecture Decision Records (ADRs). Contribute to incident response, technical interviews, quarterly planning, and occasional customer-facing technical discussions. Requirements 10+ years of backend engineering experience , including several years in architecture or technical leadership roles at the principal level. Deep, hands-on expertise in C# and .NET, with a proven track record of designing and delivering secure, scalable, and resilient commercial backend systems. Practical experience with Azure services, particularly Azure Functions, Azure Service Bus, and Azure Data Factory. Experience working with PostgreSQL, Cosmos DB, Snowflake, CI/CD pipelines, and DevOps practices. Demonstrated success incrementally decomposing large monolithic systems, prioritizing safe, reversible changes over disruptive rewrites. Strong understanding of event-driven and asynchronous architectures, including message ordering, idempotency, poison messages, retries, and dead-letter queues. Extensive experience with API design, service contracts, versioning, and backward compatibility. Strong data-access fundamentals, including query optimization, zero-downtime migrations, and handling inconsistent or complex customer data. Proven production ownership, including observability, alerting, incident response, and root-cause analysis. Required: Daily, hands-on use of AI development tools such as Claude, Claude Code, or comparable agentic engineering tools, along with practical experience building AI-powered solutions involving agents, reusable skills, MCP servers, or evaluations. Excellent written and spoken English, with the ability to communicate complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences. A pragmatic engineering mindset, strong judgment, and a demonstrated ability to elevate the engineers and teams around you. What We're Looking For This opportunity is specifically for a true Principal-level engineer, not simply a strong Senior Engineer . The ideal candidate has personally owned significant architectural decisions in production environments, influenced engineering practices across multiple teams, and successfully guided complex technical transformations without relying on formal management authority. Candidates must be able to provide concrete examples of architectural decisions they personally made, the trade-offs involved, and the measurable outcomes. Experience leading the incremental decomposition of a large monolith is particularly valuable. High-level architectural knowledge alone will not be sufficient. The client is highly selective and is looking for someone who can demonstrate both deep technical expertise and a clear record of architectural ownership while continuing to write production code. Why Join? Real architectural ownership: Shape the backend architecture of a business-critical software platform. Technical influence: Help define engineering standards and guide technical decisions across multiple teams. Hands-on impact: Stay close to the code while leading complex architectural initiatives. AI-forward engineering: Help shape how a growing engineering organization integrates AI into its everyday development practices. Collaborative environment: Work alongside experienced architects and engineers who value thoughtful technical decisions and continuous improvement. Engagement Details Full-time, remote independent contractor engagement. Compensation of $45–$50 USD per hour , depending on experience and fit. Timesheet submission is required. Days off, sick days, and local holidays are not billable. Working on local holidays may be possible by prior arrangement. Company hardware will be shipped to the selected candidate. The anticipated start date is approximately four weeks after the offer is signed. Application Process Our recruitment team will carefully evaluate candidates' technical depth, architectural ownership, hands-on engineering experience, and practical use of AI development tools. Please highlight specific production examples of architectural decisions you've owned, large-scale backend transformations you've led, and how you've influenced engineering teams without formal authority. Only candidates who meet the principal-level requirements and can demonstrate the required experience will be presented to the client. Originally posted on Himalayas

description: Senior Software Engineer, Front End – Dashboard About Caliza Caliza is commercial banking infrastructure for companies that operate across borders. Most global businesses still piece together several banks, FX providers and spreadsheets to move money. Caliza replaces that with one platform and API: hold USD accounts, collect and pay in 33+ currencies, and convert between fiat and stablecoins, over local rails, SWIFT or stablecoins, in minutes instead of days. On top of that, we’re building the treasury layer: programmable accounts, approval policies, automated reconciliation and working capital, run by a customer’s finance team or their AI agents. Our customers are importers, exporters, FX brokers, payment companies and fintechs across the Americas, Europe, Africa and Asia. We’re licensed and regulated across our core markets, and our team has built financial infrastructure at Visa, Nubank, EBANX, Flutterwave, Upstart, Intuit and Silicon Valley Bank. Our backers Initialized Capital, Better Tomorrow Ventures, Abstract Ventures, New Form Capital, QED Investors, Valor Capital and Quona Capital, along with the founders of Flutterwave, Chipper Cash, Rappi, Pomelo, Dock, Remesa Online and Anchorage. About the role The Caliza dashboard is where our customers see and control money moving across rails, currencies and countries. When a payment is in flight, a balance changes, or a compliance check is pending, the dashboard has to show it accurately and immediately, even across thousands of transactions. As a Senior Software Engineer focused on the dashboard, you'll own features end to end, including transaction and settlement views, balances across currencies, search and filtering, exports and reporting, and the permissions that control who sees and does what. You'll work closely with design, product, back-end and compliance. Location: Remote, open to candidates based in Latin America. Professional English required. In your first six months, you'll Design and build the real-time dashboard experience, so customers see payment and balance changes as they happen. Make large transaction tables fast and usable, with solid filtering, search and export. Improve how we show payment and settlement state, so users always know where money is and what happens next. Strengthen our shared component library and set front-end conventions for testing, performance and accessibility. What you'll be doing Build and maintain the dashboard in TypeScript and React. Design data-dense interfaces: tables, detail views, charts and reports. Integrate with back-end APIs, handling the loading, error and edge-case states that matter when money is involved. Contribute to our back-end services in Kotlin and Spring Boot when a feature needs it, such as adding or changing the APIs the dashboard depends on. Implement role-based access so each user sees exactly what they should. Own performance, from rendering large data sets to efficient data fetching. Write meaningful automated tests and review your teammates' code. Work with product and design from early concept through launch. What we're looking for 5+ years of professional front-end development experience. Deep expertise in TypeScript and React. Experience with data fetching, caching and state management tools such as Redux Toolkit and TanStack Query. Experience building real-time interfaces (websockets, live updates). Comfort working across the stack: you're happy to make back-end changes when a feature needs them. Experience building data-heavy applications such as dashboards, admin tools or analytics products. Strong product sense: you care about building rich, highly usable interfaces, not just shipping tickets. A strong grasp of front-end security: handling sensitive data, XSS/CSRF protection, and secure authentication flows. Real experience writing automated tests and caring about test quality. Hands-on experience with AI-assisted development in your daily work, with the judgment to review and question what the tools produce. Solid understanding of performance and accessibility (WCAG). Comfort with high autonomy and ambiguity in a fast-moving, remote startup. Clear written communication. Most of our collaboration is async. Nice to have Experience in fintech, payments, banking or crypto products. Back-end experience with Kotlin or Java and Spring Boot. Experience building or maintaining a design system. Experience with multiple currencies, languages, and number and date formats. How we work We use AI coding tools every day and expect you to as well. They make us faster at the routine parts of the work. But you own every line you ship: you understand it, test it, and can defend it in review. Because we handle financial data, we follow clear rules about what code and data can go into which tools. title: Development Team Lead
description: This is a remote position. This is a UK Based remote role, you must have the right to work in the UK. Kyckr is a fast-scaling SaaS and data company transforming how financial crime teams verify businesses. We give regulated institutions, including banks, fintechs, law firms and payment providers, access to legally authoritative company data from 300+ corporate registries across 120 countries. Our customers use Kyckr to power their Know Your Business (KYB) and AML workflows, helping them onboard customers, assess risk and maintain ongoing compliance with confidence. We've been a trusted name in the market for 20 years, but we operate like a scale-up. Our team is small, decisions are made quickly, and we're always improving what we build. After a year of record growth, we are investing in our engineering team to accelerate delivery of our next-generation Registry Hub architecture. We are a small, focused engineering team distributed across Australia, the UK, and the Philippines. We operate on Azure, run a large .NET monorepo alongside a newer microservices architecture, and are actively adopting AI-assisted development tooling — including Claude Code and GitHub Copilot — as a core part of how we build software. We are looking for a Development Team Lead to lead a small team of four developers while remaining a hands-on senior engineer. This is a player-coach role: we anticipate roughly an 80/20 split between writing code and leading the team. You will spend the majority of your time building software, and the rest growing your engineers, unblocking delivery, and raising the technical bar. You will be one of our most senior technical contributors — setting the standard for code quality, design, and AI-assisted ways of working — at the same time as owning the line management and career development of your team. You will report directly to the CTO and work closely with them on technical direction, delivery, and team growth. Two areas matter especially for this role. First, agentic AI for coding: we are not experimenting at the edges — Claude Code and agentic development and QA workflows are central to how we build, and we want a leader who can drive that adoption from the front. Second, product integrations: a large part of our value is connecting reliably to corporate registries and third-party data sources worldwide, and to our customers’ systems, so deep, practical integration experience is important. The right person is an excellent engineer who genuinely enjoys developing people, communicates clearly in a distributed team, and is energised by working in a domain where data quality has real regulatory consequences. What You’ll Be Doing Hands-On Engineering (the majority of your time) Spend most of your time writing clean, testable, production code in .NET (C#) and SQL Server across our monorepo and newer Registry Hub services — leading by example, not from the sidelines. Take on the most complex and ambiguous technical work, and set the standard for design, code quality, and testing across the team. Own significant features and services end-to-end, from design through delivery and operation. Lead architecture and design discussions, making pragmatic, well-reasoned decisions and clearly communicating the trade-offs. Agentic AI for Coding Drive the team’s use of Claude Code and agentic development and QA workflows — for code generation, refactoring, test writing, code review, automated regression checking, and code analysis. Define and continuously improve the prompt engineering practices, agent configurations, and guardrails that let the team build faster without compromising quality. Evaluate and introduce new AI tooling as the landscape evolves, and help the wider engineering organisation adopt what works. Establish how we measure the impact of AI-assisted development on velocity and quality, and use that to guide adoption. Product Integrations Lead the design and delivery of integrations with third-party registry APIs and data sources, handling the complexity of varied data formats and reliability characteristics across 120 countries. Own the patterns for resilient, observable, and maintainable integrations — retries, error handling, rate limiting, and monitoring. Work with product and customer-facing teams to deliver integrations into customers’ systems and workflows that solve real compliance problems. Team Leadership & People Management Line-manage a team of four developers, including regular one-to-ones, performance management, and active career development and growth planning. Mentor and coach engineers, giving and receiving constructive feedback through code review and day-to-day collaboration. Own your team’s delivery — planning, prioritisation, and removing blockers — in partnership with product and the CTO. Foster a pragmatic, high-trust, high-ownership engineering culture and help recruit and onboard new engineers as the team grows. Delivery, Quality & Collaboration Champion strong engineering practices: meaningful tests, safe and repeatable deployments through our Azure DevOps CI/CD pipelines, and continuous improvement. Work asynchronously with a distributed team across three time zones, using Microsoft Teams, Azure DevOps, Confluence, and Jira. Document technical decisions, architecture, and runbooks clearly — good written communication matters in a remote team. Collaborate with product, compliance, and customer success to understand requirements and deliver solutions that meet real-world needs Requirements We are looking for 7–10 years of hands-on software development experience, including time spent leading or mentoring other engineers. The ideal candidate will have held a formal “Team Lead” title before. You should be ready to combine deep, current technical contribution with real responsibility for a team. You don’t need to have worked in FinTech or RegTech specifically, but you should be comfortable building production services where reliability and security matter. Essential 7–10 years of professional software development experience, with strong, current hands-on skills in .NET / C#. Solid experience with SQL Server: queries, stored procedures, and relational data modelling. Proven experience designing, building, and consuming RESTful APIs and integrating with third-party systems and data sources. Experience with Microsoft Azure services (Azure Functions, App Services, Service Bus, Blob Storage, Key Vault, APIM). Demonstrable experience leading, mentoring, or line-managing engineers — and a genuine interest in developing people and their careers. Hands-on experience with AI-assisted and agentic development tooling (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or similar), and enthusiasm for making it central to how a team works. Strong system design and architecture judgement, with the ability to make and clearly explain pragmatic trade-offs. Excellent problem-solving and debugging skills across a distributed system. Strong written and verbal communication for a remote, distributed team. Comfortable balancing hands-on delivery with leadership responsibilities (an 80/20 coding-to-leadership split). Nice to Have Experience configuring or operating agentic AI workflows for development or QA at a team level. Exposure to CI/CD pipelines and DevOps practices (Azure DevOps, YAML pipelines, automated deployments). Experience with message-driven and event-driven architectures (Azure Service Bus, queues). Familiarity with containerisation (Docker) and Kubernetes. Front-end experience with React or other modern JavaScript/TypeScript frameworks. Experience working in a regulated industry (FinTech, HealthTech, GovTech, or similar). Benefits Remote-first with periodic in person collaboration days Annual leave + UK bank holidays (25 days + 8 bank holidays) Private Medical Insurance Enhanced maternity/paternity leave Supportive family & sick leave policies Best-in-class pension contributions Annual training budget Laptop + home office equipment provided as required Work from Anywhere: up to 20 days/year (policy conditions apply) Wellbeing programme + quarterly socials Originally posted on Himalayas

title: Engineering Manager, Automation Intelligence
description: Fingerprint empowers enterprises to detect and stop online fraud with the world’s most accurate device intelligence. We lead our industry with bleeding-edge identification capabilities and work on turning new ideas and discoveries in the fraud detection space into reality. Our customers range from innovative startups to leading enterprise companies, including Plaid, Dropbox, and Booking.com. Fingerprint is a globally dispersed, 100% remote company. We were named on on the 2026 Forbes Best Startup Employers list and ranked #803 on the 2026 Inc. 5000 list of America’s fastest-growing private companies. We have raised $77M and are backed by Craft Ventures (Tesla, Facebook, Airbnb ), Nexus Venture Partners ( Postman, Apollo.io,MinIO, Druva) and Uncorrelated Ventures ( Redis, Rollbar, Gradle). The Role in Context Fingerprint 's device intelligence platform processes billions of identification events for companies that need to know who — or what — is on the other end of a request. Increasingly, the answer is not a person. AI agents, AI assistants, crawlers, headless browsers, and malicious automation now make up a large and fast-growing share of internet traffic, and telling them apart from humans — and from each other — is becoming one of the most important problems our customers ask us to solve. We are standing up a dedicated Automation Intelligence engineering team to own that problem end to end: detection in the browser, detection at the edge, the classification taxonomy that tells customers what kind of automation they're seeing and how confident we are, and the API that customers and their agents call. We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead this team. You'll inherit a small, senior group (three engineers to start, growing to four or five) and a clear mandate. You report directly to the VP of Engineering. Your Mission Ship the product — Take the automation intelligence product through Beta to GA, and then to a standalone commercial launch. You own engineering readiness: scope, estimates, service reliability, operating limits, API and MCP coverage, and the evidence that it's ready Make detection accurate and keep it that way — Build the team's quality loop: a test corpus of known bots, agents, and automation frameworks; continuous false-positive and false-negative testing; a regression test for every confirmed gap; and coverage benchmarked against the best in the industry. Detection quality is the product Build a team that runs itself — Set the team up so adding a detection, shipping a change, or running a staged rollout doesn't depend on another team's calendar. Grow the engineers, hire the next seats, and create an environment where senior people do their best work Lead the AI-native engineering model — AI agents write the code by default and engineers decide what gets built and whether it's right. You'll operate that model, measure it honestly, and produce the playbook the rest of engineering adopts What You'll Do Delivery & Product Readiness Own the engineering plan for Beta → GA → standalone launch: PRD partnership with the product manager, estimates, sequencing, and the readiness evidence that gates each stage Define and prove the service's operating envelope — throughput, latency tails, rate limiting, availability SLOs — before customers depend on it Run staged rollouts for detection changes that affect customer bot rates, with feature flags, rollback, and clear go/no-go evidence for customer-facing teams Turn design-partner feedback and customer-reported false positives into prioritized, owned engineering work Detection Quality & Coverage Stand up and run a weekly detection quality loop: prioritized test corpus, automated FP/FN testing across browser and edge detection, regression coverage, and drift monitoring Drive coverage of the automation that matters most to customers — AI agents and assistants first — benchmarked against industry leaders, and prioritized by customer exposure rather than catalogue size Guide the hard problems: self-hosted agents, stealth and anti-detect browser automation, and fingerprinting agent infrastructure across browser, network, and runtime evidence Evolve the classification contract from "automation detected" to rich agent context — automation type, verified vs. inferred identity, confidence, and reason codes — and keep detection and attribution measured separately Team Leadership Manage, coach, and grow a team of senior engineers; run hiring for the next seats, starting with a detection research and quality engineer Set the team's goals against its charter and bring them to leadership for alignment, not approval; communicate decisions as intent with reasoning before acting Establish healthy engineering practice from day one: written ownership lines, review tiers per repository, specs before epics, and baselines for cycle time, throughput, predictability, change failure rate, and recovery time Negotiate clean working agreements with the sibling team the codebase is shared with today, and drive gradual decoupling prioritized by what blocks independent deploys AI-Native Engineering Operate the agent-first development model: spec → coding agent → review agent → security review → human merge, with low-risk changes merging on agent approval and mandatory human review on critical paths Treat the agent harness — repository instructions, skills, review personas — as infrastructure maintained like code, and publish it so other teams start ahead Measure the model against the team's own baseline, run 30- and 60-day reviews, and write up what worked and what didn't for the rest of engineering Contract-First APIs Ensure every surface the team ships is contract-first: OpenAPI in the repo, breaking-change detection in CI, generated docs and SDKs, and the API kept readable by both developers and AI agents Own the team's observability: logs, metrics, traces, and SLOs for the detection service What We're Looking For Required Engineering management experience: 3+ years managing software engineers, ideally including senior and staff-level ICs, with a track record of shipping products — not just features — through launch Strong technical foundation: 8+ years in software engineering before or alongside management. You can read a design doc and a PR critically, engage senior engineers on architecture, and make technical calls when the team is split Relevant domain depth in at least one of: bot detection or bot management, fraud or abuse prevention, web security, browser or client-side engineering, or high-volume API services. You understand that this is an adversarial problem where the other side adapts Quality-driven mindset: Experience building or running measurement-driven engineering — test corpora, precision/recall or FP/FN tracking, regression suites, SLOs — and using that data to prioritize Hands-on with AI coding tools: You use AI coding agents in your own work, have opinions about where they help and where they don't, and are excited to lead a team where they are the default Cross-functional operator: You've worked closely with product managers, researchers, and customer-facing teams, and you're comfortable making dependencies and trade-offs explicit rather than absorbing them Clear communicator: You write well, make decisions visible with your reasoning, and can explain detection quality and launch readiness to executives and customers alike Nice to Have Direct experience with bot detection, bot management, or anti-automation products (e.g. at a CDN, WAF, fraud, or security vendor) Familiarity with AI agent ecosystems : agent frameworks, verified-agent protocols, and how agents interact with websites and APIs Experience with browser internals or headless/automation frameworks and the techniques used to detect or evade them Experience running API-first products with public OpenAPI specs, SDKs, and MCP or similar agent-facing surfaces Experience forming a new team out of an existing one — separating codebases, setting ownership lines, and keeping the sibling relationship healthy Experience in a high-growth SaaS company with enterprise customers The Shape of This Role This is a hands-on-adjacent engineering manager role for a small, senior, high-leverage team. You are not expected to write the production code — your engineers and their agents do that — but you are expected to be close enough to it to set direction, evaluate the work, and hold the quality bar. The team has unusual autonomy and unusual visibility. It owns a product that leadership considers strategically critical, it is the first team operating Fingerprint 's AI-native engineering model, and its results — good and bad — will be used as evidence for how the rest of engineering works. That means two things: you'll have real room to decide how the team operates, and you'll need to be honest about what the data shows. In the first 90 days you will likely: finalize the roster and ownership lines with the sibling team, get the quality loop and engineering baselines running, deliver the engineering evidence for the Beta gate, and run the first review of the AI-native operating model. Why This Role? A problem that is getting harder and more important every quarter: The internet is filling with agents. Customers need to tell useful automation from abuse, and the answer isn't "block everything." The team that solves this well defines a category A product with a clear path to market: Beta to GA to standalone launch, with product, go-to-market, and executive support already lined up A senior team and a dedicated PM from day one: You're not starting from zero. The engineers already know the problem; your job is to focus them and remove what's in their way Lead how engineering will work next: AI-native development, contract-first APIs, and a self-directed team model — piloted here first, with your findings shaping the whole organization VP direct line: You report to the VP of Engineering, set your own goals against a clear charter, and bring recommendations rather than requests for direction Compensation & Transparency At Fingerprint , we believe in pay transparency — it's part of how we operate as a distributed, remote-first team. Salaries are based on function, level, and geographic location, benchmarked against similar stage growth companies. Because this role is open across the United States and can be based anywhere our team members work from, the salary range reflects that geographic breadth: $159k - $215k Some example salaries for specific locations are below: NYC: $187k - $215k Chicago: $159k - $183k Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors, including the successful candidate's location, experience, and expertise, and may vary from the amounts listed above. Due to regulatory and security reasons, there’s a small number of countries where we cannot have Fingerprint teammates based. Additionally, because Fingerprint is an all-remote company and people can join our workforce from almost any country, we do not sponsor visas. Fingerprint teammates need to be authorized to work from their home location. We are dedicated to creating an inclusive work environment for everyone. We embrace and celebrate the unique experiences, perspectives and cultural backgrounds that each employee brings to our workplace. Fingerprint strives to foster an environment where our employees feel respected, valued and empowered, and our team members are at the forefront in helping us promote and sustain an inclusive workplace. We highly encourage people from underrepresented groups in tech to apply. If you are applying as a resident of California, please read our CCPA notice here. If you are applying as a resident of the EU, please read our GDPR notice here. **We have noticed a rise in recruiting impersonations across the industry, where scammers attempt to access candidates' personal and financial information through fake interviews and offers. All Fingerprint recruiting email communications will always come from the @fingerprint.com domain. Any outreach claiming to be from Fingerprint via other sources should be ignored. title: Software Designer (UI/UX)
description: Job Overview: We are seeking an experienced UX Designer who is passionate about creating user-centered digital experiences across web and mobile platforms. As a UX Designer, you will play a critical role in our product development process, working closely with product owners, stakeholders, and development teams to deliver seamless and impactful designs. Key Responsibilities: User Research and Analysis: Conduct user research using various methods, including user interviews, surveys, usability testing, and data analysis. Analyze user feedback and behavioral data to identify user needs, pain points, and opportunities for improvement. Develop user personas, journey maps, and user flows to guide design decisions. Design and Prototyping: Create wireframes, prototypes, and high-fidelity UI designs for web and mobile platforms using Figma. Design user interfaces following best practices for usability, accessibility, and responsive design. Leverage design systems to ensure consistent design across products. Collaborate closely with Product Owners and stakeholders to gather requirements, align on goals, and ensure design feasibility. Stakeholder Management: Present and defend design concepts to stakeholders, including product owners, developers, and management. Act as a bridge between design, development, and business teams, ensuring alignment and clarity throughout the design process. Facilitate design review sessions, gathering feedback and iterating on designs. Business Requirements and Design Validation: Work directly with Product Owners to understand business requirements and translate them into intuitive user experiences. Ensure that designs align with business goals while maintaining a user-centered approach. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to validate designs and ensure successful implementation. Continuous Improvement: Stay up-to-date with the latest UX/UI design trends, tools, and best practices. Continuously iterate on designs based on user feedback and analytics. Contribute to the maintenance and evolution of the design system for scalability. Requirements: Education and Experience: Bachelor's degree in UX Design, Graphic Design, Human-Computer Interaction, or a related field. 2+ years of experience in UX/UI design, preferably with experience across the full product design lifecycle. Proven experience designing for web and mobile platforms. Strong portfolio showcasing UX/UI design work, including design systems and complex interfaces. Technical Skills: Proficiency in Figma for design and prototyping. Solid understanding of design systems and how to leverage them for consistent, scalable designs. Experience working with Product Owners to gather and translate business requirements into design solutions. Familiarity with user-centered design principles, usability testing, and accessibility best practices (WCAG). Basic knowledge of front-end technologies (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) is a plus. Interpersonal Skills: Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to explain design concepts to stakeholders of varying technical backgrounds. Collaborative mindset and ability to work effectively in cross-functional teams. Proactive and solution-oriented, with strong problem-solving skills. Preferred Qualifications: Experience working in Agile or Scrum environments. Familiarity with accessibility standards (WCAG). Experience with design systems in a scalable environment. title: Senior Motion Planning Engineer - Safety-Layer
description: Mission Summary: The Safety-Layer Team is responsible for ensuring the Motional Autonomous Vehicle executes appropriate dynamic trajectories in both nominal and safety-critical scenarios. This team focuses on refining upstream motion plans to guarantee compliance with safety-driven requirements, executing highly dynamic evasive maneuvers at the AV’s physical limits, and implementing system-wide safety overrides. The team pursues these goals through a process of rigorous algorithmic design, implementation, validation, analysis in simulation, and comprehensive closed-course and public road evaluation. As the team's responsibilities are growing to support more complex scenarios and the scaling of Motional ’s deployment area, we are looking for a Senior Motion Planning - Safety-Layer to help build a robust motion planning safety-layer. You will work on enabling cutting-edge capabilities for Motional ’s AV, including algorithm design and documentation, software development, metrics definition, simulation implementation and evaluation, and in-vehicle testing. As part of this role, you will maintain cross-functional relationships across the organization to help understand and communicate the impacts of their work on overall AV performance. What you will work on: Design, implement, and test algorithms for synthesizing trajectories and selecting trajectories across asynchronous generation sources to ensure AV behaviors adhere to safety-critical requirement specifications. Develop evasive maneuver planning algorithms in conjunction with low-level control systems to safely use the full actuation capacity of Motional ’s AV for collision avoidance. Evaluate the role of multiple perception sensor modalities in refining the safety-layer’s identification of safety-critical scenarios. Construct test/analysis tooling for isolated and system-level evaluation of safety-layer components and processes, select test parameters, and analyze test results. Utilize, validate, and improve dynamic simulation environments to accelerate the design and analysis of safety-critical motion planning algorithms, including validating simulation models against real-world data. Define and implement performance, comfort, and safety metrics for motion planning and safety systems, and perform quantitative analysis of fleet-wide vehicle data to validate design improvements and identify key areas of improvement. Build a system-wide understanding of Motional ’s autonomy stack components by supporting root-cause analysis of simulation, closed-course, and public road events from a motion planning and safety perspective. Travel for in-person vehicle testing at Motional ’s and our partner's deployment and test track locations, typically once every 4 to 6 months. Desired Background: MS, PhD preferred, in one of Control Theory / Robotics / Computer Science / Applied Math or a related field 3+ years of experience developing motion planning and collision avoidance related algorithms and components in an industrial setting, preferably the AV industry Strong background in modern C++ programming (C++17, C++20), with an emphasis on developing high-performance and reliable systems Experienced with concepts from motion planning including trajectory generation through numerical optimization and sampling-based approaches, cost and heuristic-based methods for trajectory selection, multi-modal prediction models, geometric and physics-based collision detection, time-series data processing, and data visualization Familiarity with dynamic collision modeling, convex set processing, state machine logic, and multi-rate decision-making processes Familiarity with agentic-based development tooling Familiarity with Linux-based operating systems Bonus Points: General familiarity with machine learning, including supervised learning, reinforcement learning, training/test validation, etc. Familiarity with vehicle dynamics modeling, including standard longitudinal/lateral vehicle dynamics models Publications in Robotics/Controls or Autonomous Driving conferences/journals (IROS, ICRA, CoRL, RAL, TRO, CDC, ACC, TAC, CSL, Automatica, IV, ITSC, T-ITS) Familiarity with SQL-based queries Familiarity with Python Familiarity with Gitlab, Bazel, VSCode / CLion Familiarity with AV industry simulation tooling The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors including but not limited to specific skills, experience and expertise, role location, certifications, licenses, and business needs. The estimated compensation range listed in this job posting reflects base salary only. This role may include additional forms of compensation such as a bonus or company equity. The recruiter assigned to this role can share more information about the specific compensation and benefit details associated with this role during the hiring process. Candidates for certain positions are eligible to participate in Motional ’s benefits program. Motional ’s benefits include but are not limited to medical, dental, vision, 401k with a company match, health saving accounts, life insurance, pet insurance, and more. Salary Range $172,000—$229,000 USD Motional is a driverless technology company making autonomous vehicles a safe, reliable, and accessible reality. We’re driven by something more. Our journey is always people first. We aren't just developing driverless cars; we're creating safer roadways, more equitable transportation options, and making our communities better places to live, work, and connect. Our team is made up of engineers, researchers, innovators, dreamers and doers, who are creating a technology with the potential to transform the way we move. Higher purpose, greater impact. We’re creating first-of-its-kind technology that will transform transportation. To do so successfully, we must design for everyone in our cities and on our roads. We believe in building a great place to work through a progressive, global culture that is diverse, inclusive, and ensures people feel valued at every level of the organization. Diversity helps us to see the world differently; it’s not only good for our business, it’s the right thing to do. Scale up, not starting up. Our team is behind some of the industry's largest leaps forward, including the first fully-autonomous cross-country drive in the U.S, the launch of the world's first robotaxi pilot, and operation of the world's longest-standing public robotaxi fleet. We’re driven to scale; we’re moving towards commercialization of our technology, and we need team members who are ready to embrace change and challenges. Formed as a joint venture between Hyundai Motor Group and Aptiv, Motional is fundamentally changing how people move through their lives. Headquartered in Boston, Motional has operations in the U.S and Asia. For more information, visit www. Motional .com and follow us on Twitter, LinkedIn, Instagram and YouTube. Motional AD Inc. is an EOE. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. To comply with Federal Law, we participate in E-Verify. All newly-hired employees are queried through this electronic system established by the DHS and the SSA to verify their identity and employment eligibility. Originally posted on Himalayas

title: Director, FP&A
description: At IEM, we’re not just building innovative electrical distribution systems, we’re shaping the future. IEM is dedicated to delivering world-class solutions for complex power needs. After 75 years, we continue to push the boundaries of what’s possible. Whether you’re an experienced professional or just starting out, you’ll have the opportunity to contribute, grow, and make a lasting impact on industries that power the world’s most dynamic markets. Location: US Remote Reports To: VP Commercial Financial Planning and Analysis Salary Range: $180,000-$205,000 Position Summary: This role is dedicated to delivering financial support to our Field Service organization. Key responsibilities include preparing monthly profit and loss (P&L) statements, analyzing trends, identifying and explaining variances against budget or forecast, developing financial key performance indicators (KPIs), and conducting financial analyses for capital investments and new initiatives. The ideal candidate will bring a minimum of five to seven years of relevant finance experience, showcasing strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and a strategic approach. title: Robotics AI Engineer
description: About Menlo Menlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it. Our mission is to make humanoid labor economically viable, turning software into physical labor at scale. We build across the full stack: hardware architecture, locomotion, autonomy, simulation, and infrastructure. We move fast, ship to real robots, and open-source everything we can. If you want your work to matter beyond a paper or a demo, this is the place. The Role As a Robotics AI Engineer, you will work at the intersection of learning and hardware, training and deploying policies that run on Asimov in the real world. This is not a research role in the traditional sense. You will be expected to get results on physical robots, not just in simulation, and to iterate fast when things break. You will work closely with the hardware, firmware, and infrastructure teams to close the loop between training and deployment. What You Will Do Design and train RL and imitation learning policies for locomotion, manipulation, or whole-body control Run experiments on physical hardware and close the sim-to-real gap through systematic debugging and domain adaptation Build and maintain simulation environments and data pipelines that support fast policy iteration Instrument robot deployments and analyze failure modes to feed improvements back into training Collaborate with hardware and firmware engineers to understand physical constraints and improve policy robustness What We Are Looking For Strong foundations in reinforcement learning or imitation learning, with hands-on experience training policies that run on real systems Comfort working directly with robots, not just simulators Proficiency in Python and familiarity with standard RL/ML frameworks (JAX, PyTorch, IsaacGym/IsaacLab, MuJoCo, or similar) An empirical, debugging-first mindset, you care about what actually works on hardware Ability to move fast and context-switch between research problems and engineering tasks Nice to Have Prior work on humanoid or legged robot platforms Experience with sim-to-real transfer techniques (domain randomization, system identification, noise injection) Contributions to open-source robotics projects Background in control theory, trajectory optimization, or dynamics Why Join Menlo The policies you train do not sit in a notebook. They run on a real humanoid, in the real world, on short feedback loops. You will see your work move physical hardware within days, not quarters. You will collaborate directly with the hardware, firmware, and infrastructure teams, with high visibility and real stakes, and everything you can open-source, you will. If you want to build the systems that turn software into physical labor, this is where it happens. A Note on AI You don't need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect everyone at Menlo to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement. When that's the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don't treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on. Equal Opportunity and Accommodations We hire talented people from a wide range of backgrounds. If you're excited about a role but don't meet every bullet, we still encourage you to apply. Menlo Research is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any legally protected characteristic. Menlo provides reasonable accommodations during the application process. If you need one, please let your recruiter know. Originally posted on Himalayas

title: Senior Software Engineer, Backend

title: Software Engineer, Backend (Mid/Senior)
description: Who We Are Imprint helps the world's best brands grow the lifetime value of their customers. We started with co-branded credit cards and rebuilt them to be smarter, more rewarding, and brand-first. We partner with companies like Crate & Barrel, Rakuten, , H-E-B, Fetch, and Shell to launch modern credit programs that deepen loyalty, unlock savings, and drive growth. But the card is just the beginning. We combine advanced payments infrastructure, intelligent underwriting, and deep customer data to create delightful and personalized experiences for members as well as efficient and profitable relationships for our brand partners. Our robust technology and world-class operations allow us and our brand partners to offer powerful financial products without becoming a bank. In the U.S., co-branded cards alone account for over $300 billion in annual spend, and most still run on decades-old legacy bank systems. Imprint is the modern alternative: flexible, embeddable, and built for how people actually pay today. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Thrive Capital, Ribbit, and Khosla Ventures, we're building a world-class team to redefine how people pay and how brands grow. If you want to move fast, solve hard problems, and own real outcomes, we want to meet you. The Opportunity Own critical financial systems end-to-end : from transaction authorization and ledger accounting, to credit decisioning, to rewards engines and payment processing. Build net-new products, not just maintain existing ones : as Imprint expands into new financial products and a deeper rewards platform, you'll design and ship systems that don't exist yet alongside improving the ones that do. Contribute to foundational platform work : invest in shared services, API infrastructure, and developer tooling that make the entire engineering team faster and more reliable. Leverage AI across the stack : from prototyping to testing to production code, learning how to leverage AI tools is a core consideration for how we work. Work across a wide cross-functional surface : product, design, infrastructure, compliance, solutions engineering, and brand partners. Move fast with real responsibility : this is a growing company where individuals drive impact, not a large org where you wait for alignment. At the senior level, you may also lead system design for your team's projects and help onboard and develop other engineers. Your Profile 3+ years of experience building production backend systems (fintech experience a plus) You've built services that handle real money, real users, or real-time decisions: and you care about getting the details right Proficiency in Go (our primary backend language), or a similar language with willingness to ramp quickly Experience using AI tools (code assistants, MCP servers, agentic workflows) to accelerate development, or genuine enthusiasm to adopt them Experience ensuring data consistency and transactional integrity across distributed systems Strong with relational databases: schema design, migrations, and query performance tuning Comfortable designing API contracts consumed by both internal frontends and external partners Experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS), CI/CD pipelines, and deployment tooling You've participated in on-call rotations and incident response, including root cause analysis You communicate clearly and collaborate naturally across product, design, and engineering teams You thrive in ambiguous environments and make pragmatic tradeoffs to keep shipping We don't expect every candidate to match every bullet. If you're excited about what we're building and confident you can contribute, we'd love to talk. Stack Go, MySQL, DynamoDB, Temporal, Kafka, Kubernetes, AWS, GitHub Actions, Datadog, Statsig. Read more about how we build at Imprint on our engineering blog: . Perks & Benefits Competitive compensation and equity packages Leading configured work computers of your choice Flexible paid time off Fully covered, high-quality healthcare, including fully covered dependent coverage Additional health coverage includes access to One Medical and the option to enroll in an FSA 20 weeks of paid parental leave for the primary caregiver and 8 weeks for all new parents Access to industry-leading technology across all of our business units, stemming from our philosophy that we should invest in resources for our team that foster innovation, optimization, and productivity Imprint is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace. Imprint is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status. Imprint welcomes talented individuals from all backgrounds who want to build the future of payments and rewards. title: AI Developer in Education
description: The University of Law is looking for an AI Developer in Education to join our Technology Enhanced Learning and Teaching team and play a hands-on role in shaping how AI is used across the University. We’re looking for someone who can look at a problem, understand what we are trying to achieve, and then work out whether AI is the right solution and, if it is, build it, test it, improve it and make it work at scale. You’ll sit at the intersection of AI development, software engineering and education , working closely with our academic and learning design teams to turn ideas into practical AI-powered tools and experiences. You’ll also work directly with our key AI technology partners, helping to shape development priorities, troubleshoot issues and make sure we are getting real value from the technology we invest in. This is an opportunity to join a University that is actively exploring what AI can do for education, while having the technical expertise and influence to help determine what should actually be built and how it should work. What will you be doing? You’ll take technical ownership of the development, configuration and optimisation of AI tools used across our educational provision. This will include: Designing, developing and maintaining Topics, Agents and Workflows within our generative AI platform, turning educational and business requirements into functional solutions. Building, testing and refining AI-powered learning experiences, using user feedback and evidence to continually improve them. Exploring emerging AI technologies and leading technical pilots and proof-of-concept projects — assessing not just whether something can be done, but whether it delivers meaningful value. Integrating AI platforms with University systems, including Blackboard Ultra , student information systems and other digital learning technologies. Working with APIs, LLMs and data integrations to create solutions that are secure, reliable and fit for purpose. Acting as a technical expert for our key AI platforms and technology partners, understanding their capabilities, limitations and development roadmaps. Troubleshooting technical issues and identifying practical ways to improve the performance, usability and reliability of our AI tools. Helping successful ideas move beyond experimentation and into sustainable solutions that can be used across the University. Producing clear technical documentation and guidance that can be understood by both technical and non-technical colleagues. Working closely with academic, learning design and professional services teams to understand their needs and translate them into effective technical solutions. Ensuring our AI development meets the University's requirements around security, accessibility, data protection and academic integrity. What are we looking for? We’re looking for someone with a strong technical foundation who is genuinely curious about what AI can do and equally interested in whether it should be used and what difference it will make. You’ll have: Demonstrable experience developing, configuring and maintaining AI tools or software applications. Strong programming skills in one or more relevant languages, such as Python or JavaScript , alongside experience working with AI/ML technologies. Hands-on experience with LLM APIs, prompt engineering and AI platforms , including chatbot or agent-based frameworks. Experience working with APIs, system architecture and data integration. Strong technical problem-solving skills and the ability to investigate, test and resolve complex issues. Experience communicating technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences and working effectively with a wide range of stakeholders. Experience producing clear, practical technical documentation. A strong understanding of data security, GDPR and technical compliance. A willingness to experiment with emerging technology, while applying sound judgement about what is genuinely useful and scalable. Experience working within higher education would be valuable, as would experience in a legal education environment, but we are particularly interested in people who can demonstrate strong technical development experience and a track record of turning new technology into practical solutions. To view the full job description click hereand its associated roles and responsibilities Why this role? AI in education is moving quickly. This role gives you the opportunity to be right in the middle of that change. You’ll have the freedom to explore new technologies, work with AI platforms and technology partners, and collaborate with people across the University to solve real problems. At the same time, you’ll have the opportunity to influence how AI develops beyond individual projects helping us understand what works, what doesn’t, and how successful solutions can be taken further. If you enjoy building things, solving problems, experimenting with new technology and working with people to turn ideas into something tangible, we’d like to hear from you. This is a full-time, permanent position and is home-based. Closing date for application is midnight 6th November 2026 Why join us? Along with a competitive starting salary of £56,000, you’ll enjoy: We provide a generous annual leave entitlement of 30 days Private Medical Scheme and Life Assurance Contributory Pension Scheme Opportunity for professional development, including course sponsorship and fee discounts Season Ticket Loans and Student Discounts Our Approach We are committed to ensuring our workforce is reflective of our diverse student population, striving to increase the representation of age, disability, gender identity and expression, religion, race, sex, sexual orientation, and socio-economic background of our employees. We’re also committed to providing adjustments to those who may require support with the recruitment process - please contact the ULaw Talent Acquisition Team at . title: AI Software Engineer
description: About us IOMETE is the sovereign data platform for the AI era. Enterprises run our data lakehouse, built on Apache Spark and Apache Iceberg, in their own trusted environment: on-premises, in their own cloud, or hybrid. It is built for regulated industries such as financial services, healthcare and government. Customer data never leaves the customer's trust perimeter, and the AI we build on it stays inside that perimeter too. Position overview We are seeking a highly skilled and motivated AI Software Engineer to join our team. We tackle a variety of exciting challenges, from connecting AI tools and models to the lakehouse to diagnosing Spark applications and troubleshooting failures. You'll build agents that run inside the customer's environment, on LLMs the customer provides or, later, on custom models we train for Spark tuning and troubleshooting. You'll also build the framework that defines those agents and the harness that runs, limits, traces and evaluates them. The AI team We are building the AI platform for the lakehouse — Lakehouse Intelligence. The team's roadmap includes, but is not limited to, the MCP Server for AI Agents, which lets AI tools query the lakehouse; the Model Gateway, through which IOMETE 's AI features call models; agents for Spark application diagnosis, troubleshooting and onboarding; and SQL AI Functions, which run language models from inside a query. Down the road, you'll also get to fine-tune and build custom models for our platform's specific needs, small enough to run inside a customer's deployment. What you'll do Contribute to and maintain IOMETE 's AI services, including the MCP Server for AI Agents, the Model Gateway, SQL AI Functions, and lakehouse-specific agents (such as Spark Application Diagnosis) and their harness. Build AI enablers: extend the IOMETE lakehouse and platform to support more AI-powered features, for example by making Spark job logs, query history and table metadata available to them. Be hands-on with Kubernetes, including the Helm charts that ship our AI services into each customer's deployment. Collaborate closely with external customer engineering teams to support integrations, troubleshoot complex issues and provide guidance for successful adoption of our platform. Participate in design discussions about agents, model access, evaluation, and overall systems architecture. Write the tests, docs and release notes for what you build. A feature is done when it has shipped with all of them. Review your teammates' work and provide feedback. What we're looking for 5+ years of professional experience in software engineering (we’re open to exceptional candidates with less experience who demonstrate deep systems knowledge and impact). Deep understanding of LLM-based systems in production – tool calling, structured output, retrieval, evaluation, and how they fail. Our AI features are written mostly in Python and Go. The data platform is built on the JVM, in Kotlin and Java, and new platform features are being built in Go. Production experience with any of these languages is a big plus, but we know strong engineers learn a new language fast.
